thread.title: Asia Markets: Asian markets surge, kick off global stock rally as China-U.S. trade tensions ease for now

author: Stocks News Feed
title: Asia Markets: Asian markets surge, kick off global stock rally as China-U.S. trade tensions ease for now
text:
Asian stock markets jumped Friday, reflecting investor relief about upcoming trade talks between China and the U.S., as well as the dollar‘s gains against a basket of major currencies including the yen.
President Donald Trump on Thursday said he had a good talk with Chinese President Xi Jinping , and that trade talks were “moving along nicely.” The two will meet formally later this month, with investors hoping a deal will be reached to ease trade tensions.
Japan’s Nikkei
 NIK, +2.56%
 recovered after Thursday’s losses to close up 2.6%. Earnings season cast a pall on some stocks though. Suzuki Motor Corp.
 7269, -2.52%
 was down 2.5%, off the worst of the day however, after its second-quarter operating profit slid 6.6% amid weaker sales in Europe, China and India — its biggest market. After a down day Thursday, telecoms rallied Friday, with Nippon Telegraph & Telephone
 9432, +6.67%
 up 6.6% and NTT DoCoMo
 9437, +4.49%
 rising 4%.
Chinese benchmarks were sharply higher amid hopes of easing the trade conflict, with the Shanghai Composite
 SHCOMP, +2.70%
 up 2.7% and the smaller-cap Shenzhen Composite
 399106, +3.43%
 advancing 3.4%. Insurers and brokerage firms led the gains while oil stocks were muted as oil prices slumped.
Hong Kong stocks surged, with the Hang Seng Index
 HSI, +4.21%
 up 4.2%. Sunny Optical
 2382, +10.27%
 jumped 10% with index heavyweight Tencent
 0700, +9.29%
 adding 9%. Auto stocks saw renewed buying with Great Wall
 2333, +7.04%
 and Geely Auto
 0175, +11.72%
 up 7% and 11% respectively. Among casino stocks , Galaxy Entertainment
 0027, +9.49%
 rose 9% and Wynn Macau
 1128, +13.24%
 gained 13%. “The attitudes of both Chinese and U.S. leaders have been productive, bringing more positivity to the meeting at the end of the month,” said UOB Kay Hian stock strategist Ivan Ip.
Apple Inc.
 AAPL, +1.54%
 component manufacturers were mostly unaffected by the tech giant’s after-hours slump following record quarterly earnings but a warning of slower holiday sales . Taiwan’s Taiex
 Y9999, +0.63%
 rose 0.6%, as Foxconn
 2354, +1.06%
 , Taiwan Semiconductor
 2330, +0.42%
 and Largan Precision
 3008, +5.70%
 all gained. South Korea’s Kospi
 SEU, +3.53%
 was up 3.5% as Samsung
 005930, +4.74%
 and SK Hynix
 000660, +6.30%
 gained.
Benchmark indexes in Singapore
 STI, +1.81%
 , Malaysia
 FBMKLCI, +0.41%
 and Indonesia
 JAKIDX, +0.07%
 were also up.
Australia’s ASX 200
 XJO, +0.14%
 was initially the one of region’s few losers, as the energy and financial sectors pulled down the index. But it, too, rebounded, to close up 0.1%. Oil Search Limited
 OSH, -1.29%
 was off 1.2% and ANZ Bank
 ANZ, -1.24%
 was off 1.2% as well. New Zealand’s benchmark index
 NZ50GR, -0.09%
 fell slightly, giving up less than 0.1%.
